turns.assistant_text:
Here are some notable AI news highlights from today:

1. **Helping caregivers use AI in everyday life**  
   OpenAI is working with community organizations to help caregivers build skills to use AI tools safely and effectively. The initiative aims to enhance caregivers' ability to manage responsibilities and focus more on the people they care for. [Read more](https://openai.com/index/helping-caregivers-use-ai-in-everyday-life).

2. **IBM and Microsoft announce a new AI agent platform**  
   IBM and Microsoft have launched a new AI agent platform aimed at transforming industry-specific processes. The platform focuses on enhancing human decision-making and creating value across businesses, moving beyond mere productivity aids to competitive advantages. [Read more](https://news.microsoft.com/source/2026/11/10/ibm-and-microsoft-announce-a-new-ai-agent-platform-designed-for-industry-specific-transformation).

3. **The AI Safety Debate Has Lost the Plot**  
   An article in WIRED discusses the complexities of AI safety, highlighting the need for better evaluation methods to assess AI's impact on society. Experts express concerns about losing control over essential institutions and the implications of AI on consciousness and social relationships. [Read more](https://www.wired.com/story/the-ai-safety-debate-has-lost-the-plot-we-asked-10-experts-what-the-real-nightmares-are).

4. **Building AI literacy on Adobe podcast**  
   Faculty from Washington State University will discuss AI literacy and skill-building in an upcoming podcast. They aim to prepare students to understand AI's capabilities and limitations while engaging them in real-world projects. [Read more](https://news.wsu.edu/news/2026/11/10/nov-18-carson-faculty-discuss-building-ai-literacy-on-adobe-podcast).

5. **Opinion on AI videos**  
   A Washington Post opinion piece reflects on the author's experience creating AI-generated videos, despite their mixed reception. The author shares their enjoyment in the creative process, emphasizing the fun aspect of working with AI. [Read more](https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2026/11/10/ai-videos-are-not-well-regarded-im-still-making-them-anyway).

These articles cover various aspects of AI, from practical applications in caregiving to discussions on safety and literacy.

items.title: Helping caregivers use AI in everyday life
items.summary:
1 of 4

> “AI is a tool for people to have more control over their lives and their families lives.. For caregivers, that can mean less time organizing schedules and searching for information, and more time focused on the people they care for. By working with trusted community organizations, we’re helping caregivers build the skills and confidence to use these tools safely and practically.”

—Chris Lehane, OpenAI’s Chief Global Affairs Officer [...] Participants will also learn how to use AI responsibly, including protecting personal information and understanding the limits of these tools. Participants will also learn when to consult healthcare professionals and how AI tools should complement, not replace, medical, legal, or financial advice.OpenAI facilitators and mentors will offer hands-on support throughout the workshops. No coding or technical background is required.

1 of 4 [...] > “The future of caregiving isn’t about replacing human connection with technology. It’s about using innovation to make care more manageable, accessible and connected. AI has real potential to help caregivers navigate information, coordinate responsibilities and reclaim valuable time, but only if we build their confidence and keep their needs at the center. This National Family Caregivers Month, we’re proud to join OpenAI Academy, the Alzheimer’s Association and the American Diabetes

items.title: IBM and Microsoft announce a new AI agent platform designed for industry-specific transformation - Source
items.summary: “AI is evolving quickly, and our focus at SEI is on applying it with intention in ways that strengthen trust, enhance human decision-making and create meaningful value across our business,” said Sneha Shah, Chief AI Strategist and Head of SEI Next. “Our work with IBM Consulting and Microsoft is helping us explore how emerging capabilities could support critical processes and be responsibly scaled over time, with the goal to create better experiences for our employees and clients. By combining [...] “Clients are no longer looking for AI that simply helps people do the same work a little faster. They want to build an agentic business,” said Mohamad Ali, Senior Vice President and Head of IBM Consulting. “Microsoft and IBM are helping organizations bring human expertise and digital labor together in a way that can scale across the enterprise, to turn AI from a productivity aid into a real competitive advantage.” [...] “Enterprise AI will be won by organizations that can turn their data, industry expertise and AI into action,” said Rodrigo Kede Lima, President, Microsoft Frontier Company. “Together, Microsoft and IBM Consulting are bringing the best of our technology and expertise, to help customers move from AI ambition to business impact faster and with confidence.”

items.title: The AI Safety Debate Has Lost the Plot. We Asked 10 Experts What the Real Nightmares Are | WIRED
items.summary: So, what—or who—will keep us safe from AI? Looking to regain some faith in humanity, I called a theologian who often meets with the AI labs. If there’s even a slim chance that we’re losing control of the essential institutions that undergird society, he said, then we should focus on foiling that. But AI raises other questions too. What does it mean to be conscious? To create? To commune with other people? The answers are “entirely up for grabs,” he said. My anxiety’s still kicking around, but I [...] Some of the scenarios that people worry about—whether it’s biosecurity or a cyberattack or some of the everyday harms like the degradation of children’s social relationships—are very complex phenomena that can’t be easily tested or modeled by looking at a system in isolation. I think almost all evaluation scientists would tell you that it’s a nascent field. We can start to provide evidence, but it’s not necessarily proof of whether an AI is safe or not. We need to get better at evaluating these [...] As someone who’s been invited to speak with multiple AI labs, I find that the experts on the frontier disagree with each other on things like recursive self-improvement, loss of control, or our ability to keep institutions like the financial system or water table or even nuclear weapons safe. items.title: Nov. 18: Carson faculty discuss building AI literacy on Adobe podcast | WSU Insider | Washington State University
items.summary:
Crossler, an expert in information systems, leads AI literacy and skill-building workshops on the WSU Pullman and Vancouver campuses with the goal of preparing students not just to use AI but to understand what it does well, where it falls short, and how to use it responsibly. [...] Robert Crossler

During the podcast, Crossler and Cooney will share their experience embedding AI fluency into foundational course work while engaging students in meaningful, team-based projects that mirror real-world business consulting work. [...] A laptop sits open on a desk with a large AI microchip icon displayed as a digital overlay above the keyboard. A hand reaches toward the screen area, surrounded by glowing blue technology icons representing artificial intelligence.

Carson College of Business faculty leaders Robert Crossler and Chris Cooney will share insights on building students' AI fluency and career skills on Adobe’s Academic Innovation Café Nov. 18 podcast (Illustration by Smile Studio AP/AdobeStock).
